ticket.title: miter deps still misses a dependency referenced only by a qualified path in some files
ticket.description:
GB-232 fixed the module-name collision, which removed four false positives. One case survives and is measured: outfeed-core declares reqwest and uses it only as `reqwest::blocking::get(&url)` and `reqwest::StatusCode::NOT_FOUND` in src/index_poll.rs, with no `use reqwest` anywhere - and `miter deps --path . --unused` still lists outfeed-core/reqwest.

This is the last item in GB-201 and the only one that would be destructive to act on: parquet was the same shape and turned out to be masked by a module name, but reqwest has no same-named module in outfeed-core, so the qualified-path branch is not firing for this file. Worth noting the diagnostic risk: a grep loop I wrote to verify candidates reported 0 hits for reqwest while a direct grep found two lines, so the harness needs a counted result (wc -l) rather than an exit code before any future purge trusts it.

NEXT: reproduce with src/index_poll.rs as the fixture - if import_roots_in_source finds reqwest there, the loss is in the walk or the filter; if it does not, the stripper is eating the file (the same suspicion that was wrong for batten-core but may be right here, since index_poll.rs also has cfg-gated code).

verification_receipt.summary: A char literal holding a double quote no longer blinds the stripper. code_only handled string and raw-string literals but not char literals, so `line.split(chr(39)+chr(34)+chr(39))` in outfeed-core/src/index_poll.rs was read as an apostrophe followed by a string opener; the stripper consumed everything to the next quote and every later reference vanished. reqwest::blocking::get at lines 63 and 71 was therefore reported as an unused dependency. skip_char_literal now distinguishes escaped literals, single-char literals including the quote-containing one, and lifetimes. Measured before: import_roots_in_source on that file returned chrono and semver and nothing after line 42. After: reqwest at 63 and 71, and miter deps --unused dropped from 4 to 3 with only the documented candle keeps left. Three earlier hypotheses had been refuted by measurement - path scan, module-name filter (GB-232), and the walk - before printing the roots of the real file pointed at the stripper. Gate: clippy -D warnings, 183 tests, fmt green.
